11. “From the time that the perpetual sacrifice is changed and the abomination of desolation is set up, there will be one thousand two hundred and ninety days.” For having said “for a time, and times, and half a time,” he saw that the blessed Daniel had not understood; so he broke the period down into days and made plain to him what he did not understand, while even so leaving the statement obscure to everyone else. The abomination of desolation is what he calls the Antichrist himself; and the change of the perpetual sacrifice is the order of the Church's liturgy, scattered and brought to a halt by that man's madness and rage. To this the divine angel adds: 12. “Blessed is he who endures and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.” He hints and indicates that after the Antichrist receives the blow sent by God, the great Elijah will go on preaching for the remaining forty-five days, and the Master will appear coming on the clouds of heaven and will crown those who have kept the possession of endurance inviolate. The Lord also says this in the holy Gospels: “But he who endures to the end will be saved.” From this too we can learn precisely that none of these things fits Antiochus. In his case he said the calamity would prevail for two thousand three hundred days, but in the case of the Antichrist for one thousand two hundred and ninety, so that the difference in time testifies to the difference in persons and events. 13. “And you,” he says, “go and rest.” That is: it is time for you to receive the end of your life. “For there are still days until the consummation is fulfilled.” That is: no little time still remains for the present order of life. Here too he clearly taught us about the consummation, and that the things foretold will take place at it. “And you will rest, and rise to your time” (though “to your lot” is more correct, as is clear from what follows) “at the end of the days.” That is: for now you must receive the common end; but you will rise, and not simply rise, but to your lot, that is, with the company of those who lived as you did. And showing when, he added: “at the end of the days.” In this way the divine archangel clearly taught us the resurrection through the blessed, thrice-blessed Daniel. Having thus completed the revelation, the prophet added: 14. “And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom; and Daniel was the king's companion and was honoured above all his friends.” Astyages was the maternal grandfather of Cyrus. When he died, and his son Cyaxares [?]…

…[?], Cyrus overthrew the kingdom of the Assyrians and Chaldeans and transferred the power of the Medes to the Persians. “He was the king's table companion,” he says, and lived with him, and was ranked above all his intimates. Having this freedom of speech, he showed him what God had foretold about him through the prophet Isaiah, and brought about the release of the people. These things, then, we have learned from the divine prophecy of Daniel. The Jews deserve to be lamented for daring to place this divine prophet outside the list of the prophets, even though they have learned the truth of the prophecy by experience. But it is evident that the Jews of today have added this blasphemy to their other impieties, trying to obscure the plain testimony to our Saviour's appearing by denying the prophecy. Yet they will gain nothing by denying this prophecy: the other prophets bear witness, and the events themselves cry out, confirming the predictions about him. That the Jews of old called the blessed Daniel a very great prophet, Josephus the Hebrew is a trustworthy witness: he did not accept the Christian preaching, yet he could not bring himself to hide the truth. In the tenth book of the Jewish Antiquities he says many other things about the blessed Daniel, and adds this as well: “For all things fell to him in extraordinary measure, as to one of the greatest prophets; during his lifetime he had honour and glory from the kings and the people, and since his death he has an everlasting memory. For the books that he wrote and left behind are still read among us even now, and from them we are convinced that Daniel spoke with God. For he not only kept prophesying future events, as the other prophets did, but also fixed the time at which they would come to pass.” And a little further on: “From the fulfilment of his predictions he wins among the people belief in his truthfulness and a reputation for divine inspiration.” And after that he says countless other such things about him. Likewise in the twelfth book of the Antiquities he again says: “The desolation of the temple came about in accordance with the prophecy of Daniel, made four hundred and eight years earlier; for he had revealed that the Macedonians would destroy it.” This is the testimony Josephus bears to the prophet. But the Jews, sick with every kind of shamelessness, are not ashamed even before their own teachers. But let us, I beg you, having received from a prophet of God foreknowledge of what is to come, make ourselves ready for

that fearful day, so that we may rise not to everlasting shame but to everlasting life. May we all attain it by the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom be glory to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.
